translations.text: An exposition he delivered one day when he saw the crowd siding with the man who deserved the curse.
He wanted them to tell him what he had repeatedly said about him, and he wanted the others to guard themselves against that man’s deeds.
God says in the scriptures that belong to him, “Children shall not die for their fathers,” and, “The fathers shall not eat sour grapes and the children's teeth be set on edge.”
Likewise, no faithful slaves will die under faithless masters, nor will the impieties of godless masters,
who worship wood and stones, come upon slaves whose hope is in God and his Christ, Jesus.
The negligence of unbelieving and oppressive masters will come upon them, and the righteousness of faithful slaves will come upon them.
There is no slavery in the place where we are going, for those who will now free themselves from slavery to sin.
Since each person will give an account of himself to God, listen to what is written: “Separate yourselves! Separate yourselves! Do not touch anything unclean!”
Do not take part in the deeds of those who are slaves of Cronus, who love Hecate and are mad about her, gazing into her face,
whose appearance is that of a prostitute, lest Jesus, who hates those people, hate you along with them.
And the holy Scripture said that the angels spoke with Lot to make him leave Sodom quickly, warning him not to perish along with them.
They are now saying to you too, O human being, through the word of God, that you should separate yourself from their sins, lest he make you like them and wipe you out along with them.
There is a foolish weakness for anyone who succumbs to it: for people like us, who say, “We love the one who gave us knowledge, Christ,”
to accept gifts of any kind at all from godless people, or, instead, to send them gifts, establishing friendship for ourselves with Christ’s enemies.
They make it plain to certain people, or to crowds of people, that they are idol worshipers, worshiping those images of demons and saying in their arrogance,
“Just as we cannot turn you into pagans, you cannot turn us into Christians.”
For whoever bows down to godless people bows down to the devil who lives in them and honors the one they serve, the serpent.
But whoever bows down to people of God bows down to God who lives in them and honors the one they serve, Jesus.
If you say, “The Lord welcomes sinners and eats with them,” then consider why he does so: so that they will believe in him, or so that they will blaspheme him?
Or if he was not going to benefit them, how could he say, “I have come to call sinners to repentance”?
Or do you not see the sign of their willingness toward the one who called them? It is this: all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to listen to him.
If you invite an unbeliever and he comes to your God’s dinner and eats from the good things of which he said, “I have prepared them,” then that is good.
If an unbeliever invites you to dinner, you too may eat with him, as your Lord Jesus did. Your cup is separate from that of the [?]
[?] of the hands that are stretched out away from [?].
They used to thresh grain when it had more chaff or was very full.
Why should I be afraid of foolish people?
They are not ashamed to say, “There is no God.”
The lawlessness of pagans will surround me—those who trust in their wealth and boast of empty hopes.
If, from the beginning, they have spread evil reports about people of God, as it is written,
it has also been said, “The righteous will be remembered forever. He will not fear an evil report.”
What will the enemies of Christ say against me, except to pour lies out of their mouths against me about all sorts of things that never happened?
As someone said, whether he was sincere or not: “When they speak against you in the houses of the rich, I tell them what is good about you.”
For before all people who hope in Jesus, there is openness toward me on their part, and only [?] toward me.
But as for those rich oppressors, they have nothing to say against me
except to say, “You turn the hearts of the poor away from us, so that they will not work [?] in fields or at any task beyond their strength.”
And they say, “He openly entered our houses and carried away the things we worship, to our shame, because we could not stop him.”
For what other punishment and what other scourge is not upon godless people, without their noticing it?
Or is this great wrath upon them not enough—that they do not know God?
But do not let any of us think this: “If only God would repay with evil those who insult us!”
Remember, then, the Lord’s patience: he did not make the tongues of those who cursed him split apart in their mouths.
And he did not make those who cursed him burst open in their midst, just as he has not withered the tongues of those who now slander him.
And he did not make the flesh of those who say, “He is not God,” fall off.
But they will indeed fall apart and split open, and their tongues will split and be torn out when the Lord Jesus shows them the day of their slaughter.
It is indeed laid down that God’s people should pray for those who persecute them.
For this reason we bless those who curse us, in accordance with the commandment of our teacher and Lord, Christ.
For if his disciples and his servants curse people because they speak evil of them, they bear guilt toward them.
But unless they themselves curse those people because they have uttered this abomination with their mouths—that the only true God is not God,
the Father of our Lord Jesus—they share in their deeds and their words.
And they share with them in their deeds and their words.
And they are liable along with them to their judgment and their curse, and to wrath and Gehenna.
If, then, these people, who have gone beyond the nature of animals, have not known God and have not understood his wonders, his powers, and all his works—
not only those on earth, which they see and hear about, but also those in heaven and everything he will do—
how will they know his people and their deeds?
Is the person who fears a mortal human being, and a son of man who withers like grass, not a laughingstock to little children without understanding, who jump and tremble when
they hear the sound of foxes or see them?
But they cannot find you guilty of anything except this alone: pursuing legal judgments against them and justice in every matter.
All the more, then, you should withdraw from Christ’s enemies and those who oppress the poor.
For the evil words that their offspring speak against us are no worse than those their father speaks about those who fight against his thoughts at all times.
And what, then, are the good words that some people will speak to us? They are no better than those Jesus, our king and our Lord, speaks into our hearts at all times.
Nor is the struggle against those who oppose us greater than the struggle against their father, the devil, against whom we fight at all times.
If it is good for brothers and friends to help one another—
for it is good when people find faithful friends and true brothers—God’s help is nevertheless greater than all these.
For this reason, these people and those others are not my concern.
Did not a governor [?], a pagan governor, dare to say, when he came here, “I really marvel that you are cheerful”?
I answered him like this: “Why should someone who has no God but Jesus not be cheerful?
Do we worship handmade idols of demons?
As the prophets said about them, ‘There is no joy for the ungodly, says the Lord God.’”
But woe to you, woe to you, assembly of calves and dogs!
upon every beast of creation, from which God's anger has not withdrawn to this day and will not until the end, because it is an assembly of the wicked.
But a gathering of calves in a street surrounded me and seized me.
The ingratitude is not hidden from Jesus, nor has he forgotten it, because they insult him and his saints within it or through them.
For they have explained their name as meaning: “She who is full of demons, whom every evil spirit has defiled,”
so that they may fulfill their desires with her. And she belongs to them, the partner of those who blaspheme against God.
rejoicing over them on the day of their rebuke,
or laughing with those who laugh at you,
because they insult God and revile his saints while you listen.
For they do not blaspheme God and his people in private rooms, but in marketplaces and in streets where there are many listeners.
I too tell you openly, in the midst of this crowd, so that the districts and the whole land may hear these words:
Cursed are those who say, “People used to [?] gods,” or, “Gods die.”
Cursed are those who say, “If God is a god, why did he not know where the devil had come from?”
They said this because they heard in Job that the King, God Almighty, asked that demon, “Where have you come from?”
They did not understand the meaning of what they heard, for God has spoken in the Scriptures on many occasions.
For if those godless people had understood, would they not have realized that people customarily threaten servants [?] and say, “Where are you coming from?” even when they know?
Just as Elisha questioned Gehazi, knowing where he had come from and what he had done, so the Lord questioned the devil threateningly:
“Where are you coming from, destroyer, liar, you who boast over weak people?
Have you then paid attention, weakling, to my servant Job? There is no one like him.
If you want to fight, advance against him.
For I have tolerated you, demon, to test my chosen ones, so that they may laugh at you because of all the humiliations you suffer at their hands,
when they overcome you—the angel who is killed, the lion and the dragon who is trampled by those whom I have granted to be girded with strength
and to be girded with power to fight against your acts of impiety.
Cursed are those who say, “If he is a god, why did he not know where Adam was?”
For they said this because they heard in Genesis, “Adam, where are you?”
They do not know that questioning takes place not about hidden deeds, but about deeds that are revealed and things that are known,
just as God asked Moses, “What is that in your hand?” And Moses acknowledged, “It is a staff.”
And just as Joseph questioned his brothers, “Who are you, and where are you from?” although he was not ignorant.
For if they had understood, they would have shut their mouths and refrained from saying these impious things—that breed of people who themselves said from the beginning, “How did God know?”
And, “Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Those who say, “If Jesus is God, why did he not know where they had put Lazarus?” are cursed.
They said this because they heard in the Gospel, “Where have you put him?”
They do not know that the Lord asked as a human being, although he is God, and that this kind of expression often occurs in conversations, especially those of human beings.
As he said, or as the Lord himself did this as a man, as it is written in Genesis, when he asked Abraham, “Where is Sarah your wife?”
Just as the angel also asked the women in the tomb, “Who are you looking for?”
The Lord also did this when he said to Mary, “Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for?”
Just as he also asked those walking to Emmaus about the things that had happened to him, “What are these things you are saying to one another as you walk along the road?”
And just as he called to the apostles and asked them, “Little children, do you have any fish?” although he knew that they had caught nothing that night.
Just as he also asked them, “How many loaves do you have?”
Did the one who blessed the loaves and multiplied them not know how many there were?
Perhaps he also did not know who had touched the edge of his clothes, so that her blood stopped flowing?
Likewise, if the wickedness of your father Satan, or its fragments, reaches into you, O pagan, and fills you still more with unbelief,
I will say, acknowledging the truth, that he not only knows that she has been bleeding for twelve years, but he knows her from the time she was in her mother’s womb.
If a potter does not know the vessel he made with his own hands during his lifetime, Jesus himself knows those whom he formed in the beginning.
Those who know that [?]
[?] the one who [?] fire and sulfur from heaven upon the people of Sodom and Gomorrah,
until he wiped them out because of their impiety, except for Lot and his children; the one who drowned Pharaoh and his multitude in the sea because of his godlessness.
Those who loved the curse, so that it would come upon them, said, “He cannot save himself from the hands of those who crucified him.”

The one who brought them all into existence; the one who made the earth open its mouth and swallow a multitude because they had sinned against him at that time, along with all those whom he destroyed in the wilderness.
These still more accursed people said, “If he is God, why did they crucify him?”
Who will be able to count the [?]
[?] all [?], just as a single one came forth from him and killed one hundred and eighty-five thousand people in a single night from the camp of multitudes of godless people.
And Moses, his chosen one, performed all these wonders in Egypt, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
And all the things he did through his servant Joshua son of Nun, the mighty one, by his power.
And his servant Elijah raised the dead.
And he also divided the waters of the Jordan.
He walked on dry ground.
He also shut up the sky for three years and six months.
And he also brought fire down from heaven by calling upon the name of the Most High.
He consumed the stones, the water, the wood, and the calves slaughtered upon them, which he had prepared as a sacrifice,
and the ground as well, which he had made like a sea, and everything around it.
And when he prayed, rainwater poured down upon the ground.
It yielded its fruit.
Likewise, his servant Elisha raised the dead.
And he struck the crowd [?].
which he did in the name of the Most High.
And the accursed people said, “It is not from God.”
So then, concerning these things, let us question the unbelievers, whose houses contain God's curse, and not in the presence of the believers, upon whose heads rests the Lord's blessing.
“Tell us, then, who is your god, you people who [?]?”
If you say that those in the sky are your gods, you are cursed,
because our Lord and our God—the God of us Christians—created them from the beginning to shine upon the earth.
And if you say of the calf and the cow and all the other animals that they are your gods, you are cursed, because the Lord of glory, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
leaving them to pull the yoke, to cultivate the soil, to be eaten, to have their milk drunk, and to provide clothing from their wool.
If you say, “The wild animals are your gods,” you are even more accursed, because the Lord God commanded them all to come into being.
But if the dog and the cat are your gods, you are still more accursed, because the Lord God says, “I am he, I am he, and there is no other besides me.”
He assigned them their tasks: the one to keep watch, and the other to catch mice.
And if the wood, the stones, the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, and all the other things you worship are your gods,
you are even more cursed, because the ruler of the whole world left them to human beings, knowing that they would take them for themselves.
Do not [?] to say, “These godless people are cursed,” while listening to words spoken by good fathers: “You must not curse any person.”
Indeed, they are not even human beings.
But if they are human beings, they are human beings who deserve to be cursed by those who say,
“We are Christians,” because they have insulted the one who created them and blasphemed against the one who [?] them.
If the serpent deserves to be cursed, the children of that serpent deserve even more to be cursed—the serpent whom the Lord cursed from the beginning because he deceived Eve
and caused Adam to stumble in paradise, just as these cursed people now cause many to stumble
and lead astray those who cannot understand that they belong to Satan.
Therefore, if Scripture says somewhere—or rather, people of God say—“Do not curse any human being,”
they mean, “Do not curse those who curse you,” in accordance with what we said earlier.
They are not saying, “Do not curse the person who insults the one who gives you glory, Christ.”
But if the saints say, speaking about the tongue, “With it we curse people,” they mean that it is the foolishness of the person
who says, “I bless God,” while cursing good and faithful people against whom no one has anything to say.
This is how they said it: “My brothers, these things should not happen this way.”
And they are not saying, “You must not curse those who have wrapped themselves in the curse like a garment.”
And the curse entered them like water, and like oil into their bones.
If they say, “But Michael the archangel, when he was speaking with the devil and disputing with him about the body of Moses, did not dare bring a slanderous judgment against him,”
do not think they are saying, “You must not curse people who sacrifice to demons.”
For I have heard some of you say, “Michael did not speak harsh words to the devil at all.”
Rather, he said, “May the Lord rebuke you!” “That is why,” they said, “it is not right to curse people who pour out libations to Cronus.”
But the statement does not mean that the great archangel spared that devil by not cursing him.
This statement [?] now, “May the Lord rebuke you,” signifies even more strongly the curse that is coming upon him.
I will not hesitate to say that he is cursed, along with his pagan children.
He is all the more cursed along with them.
They are cursed along with him.
Or do you not see that this is not so?
What, then, is it but a curse and an insulting judgment?
Quite apart from what the Scriptures have said, these ignorant, fruitless, impure people are actually indignant,
because they speak about things they do not understand, like these other accursed people today who resemble them in blaspheming the greatness of God, because they know neither him nor his works.
Listen now, so that we may understand that we alter the words the saints wrote, bringing them into line with our own desires and making them resemble us, because we do not want sound teaching.
And so that we may understand that they are speaking about people, they compared them to empty clouds driven along by the wind,
and to dry, fruitless trees that have died a second time in their roots, and to fierce waves of the sea that cast up their shame,
and to wandering stars for which dense darkness has been prepared forever, because they dare to say things that are improper and that they do not understand.
You see that they do not find fault with those who pour out curses on people who disbelieve everything written in the Scriptures:
the things that the Lord God did and the things that his saints did in his name.
So now it says about them, “Likewise these others dream their dreams.
They defile flesh, reject authorities, and slander glorious beings.”
They rebuke the offspring of the ungodly at all times, down to these accursed people of today: “They insult things they do not understand.”
“But in the things they understand by animal instinct, they are destroyed.”
God of hosts, the Almighty, whose glory, wonders, and good gifts have filled the whole inhabited world.
Yet they reject him and blaspheme him.
But these accursed people are slaves to the crooked devil, whose wonders have filled the whole earth.
Through him they are destroyed in every kind of lawlessness.
The house of God, the church, which shines upon the whole earth and is filled with living words.
Their houses, however, which have become hosts to
demons and are filled with books of deception—through every kind of deceit they are destroyed in them.
But I return again to say that Satan is not the only one against whom the great archangel Michael brings a slanderous judgment,
but also those who have fallen away from him on the straight path.
It was also said, “The angels did not bring a slanderous judgment against them,” just as it was also written about the people who turned aside and became worthless
and went after flesh because they despised authority, being audacious and self-willed:
They do not tremble before glory, but speak insults, whereas the angels, who are greater in strength and power, do not bring an insulting judgment against them.
But these were born like irrational animals, to be captured and destroyed, slandering things they do not understand.
“They will perish in their corruption and be destroyed, having received the wages of injustice, considering their daytime luxury a pleasure.
They are audacious and defiled, living in luxury and delighting in their deceptions, their eyes full of adultery.”
And they do not stop sinning, deceiving those who are not firmly established. They have trained themselves—or rather their hearts—in acts of injustice. They are children of the curse.
I said again: Stop cursing those who have perished because of their foolishness. Stop bringing a slanderous judgment against them, or slandering them.
Therefore, if they say, “Michael the archangel did not bring a slanderous judgment against them,”
and, “The angels do not bring a slanderous judgment against these others,” they are not showing respect for Satan and those who followed them.
Who among those capable of killing a dragon that has killed many with its venom would spare it?
Rather, understand correctly what he uttered.
But this expression, “a slanderous judgment,” which he did not dare bring against the devil
or against the others who do his evil deeds, expresses a thought of this kind: he did not dare say, “If only the Lord God had never brought him into existence at all,
if you were destined to change like this through your apostasy and become a devil!
And if only he had not brought into existence the people who chose to have the minds of animals—the pagans, the barbarians, and every godless heretic!”
If only he would destroy you with his angels before the appointed time, pouring out all his anger upon you,
and unleashing all his wrath upon those who loved your alien voice and followed you,
rather than listening to the voice of the one who came into the world to rescue them—Jesus—and to save them from their ungodliness.
This is the slanderous judgment that absolutely none of the children of God, from angels to human beings, will dare to pronounce.
Indeed, a thought of this kind belongs to grumbling people, who find fault with God without cause—God, whose goodness extends to all the things he has made.
Even if they changed and mingled their true resolve with them,
they did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against them, as the pagans and heretics now dare to utter things that are improper.
